researchQuestion: Can structural/market/accounting distress measures and recovery-state information identify equity tail risk without conflating default probability, loss severity and already-priced distress?

decomposition.PD: Probability/intensity of default over a defined horizon; model- and horizon-specific.
decomposition.LGD: Loss given default conditional on default; not equal to PD.
decomposition.Recovery: Value recovered by creditors conditional on default/restructuring; depends on seniority, collateral, cycle and process.
decomposition.DistressState: A broader pre-default condition inferred from accounting/market/funding variables; not proof of default.
decomposition.EquityTailRisk: Conditional downside/crash/near-zero equity outcome; linked to but not identical to creditor loss.

modelFamilies.semantics: Equity is treated as an option on firm assets; distance-to-default depends on market equity value/volatility, liabilities, rate and horizon assumptions.
Default is modeled as a hazard/intensity process from market/state variables; recovery must be specified separately.
Coverage, leverage, profitability, liquidity and market variables can form distress scores but require PIT vintages and redundancy controls.

evidenceAndCounterevidence.support: Structural distance-to-default measures capture leverage and equity volatility and are linked to financial vulnerability.
evidenceAndCounterevidence.counter: Model assumptions about asset value/volatility, liability horizon and barrier can materially change estimates.

evidenceAndCounterevidence.support: Recovery rates vary with market frictions and macro states.
evidenceAndCounterevidence.counter: Constant recovery assumptions can materially distort defaultable-debt valuation.

evidenceAndCounterevidence.support: Some studies find high distress risk predicts weak stock returns.
evidenceAndCounterevidence.counter: The distress-return literature is mixed; issuance, mispricing, risk shifting and sample definition can subsume or reverse apparent effects.

evidenceAndCounterevidence.support: Default clusters and credit spreads co-move with cycles.
evidenceAndCounterevidence.counter: Credit spreads often exceed realized expected default losses because liquidity/risk premia matter.

pitContract: Distance-to-default inputs must use contemporaneously known equity market cap, equity volatility, liabilities and risk-free rate; no later restated balance sheets.
Define horizon, default barrier and liability mapping before outcomes are opened.
PD and recovery/LGD are separate outputs; never infer one mechanically from the other.
Actual default/restructuring/recovery events require event-time lineage and delisted/defaulted firms must remain in historical universes.
Censored/no-default observations and missing recoveries must be handled explicitly; surviving firms cannot define the whole sample.
falsificationGates: Low distance-to-default != certain default and high distance-to-default != safety.
Distress risk != guaranteed negative future stock return; pricing, optionality and risk-shifting can alter equity payoff.
Recovery is state/seniority/collateral dependent and cannot be fixed at one universal percentage.
Do not count D07 leverage, D22-02 coverage, D22-03 net debt and D22-06 spread again as separate votes if they are inputs to one distress model.
If the distress transform adds no incremental value beyond its primitive inputs, classify REJECTED_OR_REDUNDANT.
next: Build a classified issuer-level Taiwan event ledger separating bankruptcy, restructuring, bond-payment default, delayed payment, covenant breach, market/trading default and non-credit delisting.
For genuine issuer credit events, attach security seniority/collateral and dated recovery evidence.
Add first-known pre-event accounting/market inputs for defaulted/delisted firms and matched surviving controls.
Preregister class-imbalance metrics, censoring, distance-to-default horizon/barrier and recovery assumptions before any outcome test.
Keep D22-12 at L2 until issuer-level default/recovery replay is independently reproducible.

maturityDecision.reason: Taiwan corporate default/transition and delisting/default-notice source routes are identified, but an issuer-level PIT default/restructuring/recovery panel including delisted/defaulted cases is not yet reproducible. Rare-event and survivorship/coverage bias would be severe if L3 were claimed from surviving/rated firms alone.
